claims.text: Local chemical ordering primarily governs the high-temperature structural and chemical stability of high-entropy nanoalloys.
Al-Ni pair correlations drive chemical clustering in Al0.1CrCoFeNi.
Enhanced local chemical order creates a stronger bonding network.
The stronger bonding network produced by local chemical order stabilizes the microstructure and retards phase transformations under thermal and mechanical stress.
The initial Al0.1CrCoFeNi nanoalloy is homogeneous and has a nearly random elemental distribution.
High-temperature annealing near 0.8Tm combined with mechanical loading can promote or reveal changes in local chemical order.
At 70–90% of the melting point, diffusion in the alloy is sufficiently active to permit the proposed ordering response.
Short-range order in Al0.1CrCoFeNi can be manifested by preferential Al-Ni correlations and associated local clustering.
High-strain compression promotes atomistic rearrangements and a clustering-to-ordering transition in Al0.1CrCoFeNi.
Thermal fluctuations are the cause of the atomistic rearrangements that develop local chemical order.
Compression-induced local chemical order lowers local free energy.
Lower local free energy from ordering preserves the FCC or BCC lattice.
Tensile stress does not promote comparable ordering and consequently makes the alloy more susceptible to disorder or phase transformation.
High-temperature compression will produce more local chemical order than tensile loading or lower-temperature processing.
Compression-induced ordering will improve retention of the desired crystal phase relative to tensile or lower-temperature controls.
Tensile loading or lower annealing temperatures produce less pronounced local chemical order and greater phase instability.
The proposed mechanism is mainly applicable to compositions similar to Al0.1CrCoFeNi under near-melting conditions and is weakened when diffusion is limited.
Atom probe tomography and high-resolution diffraction can quantify the proposed local-order parameters and phase fractions.

contradictions.description: The intervention and conditions describe annealing with simultaneous mechanical loading, whereas the falsification design specifies annealing followed by mechanical loading.
Tensile loading is presented as a controlled intervention arm but is also described as processing without the intervention.
